question: What is the supported minimal Python interface for deterministic MuJoCo candidate rollouts and Cartesian force application?
search_queries: official MuJoCo Python bindings MjModel MjData mj_step
official MuJoCo xfrc_applied force torque layout

sources.title: MuJoCo Python bindings documentation
claims: The canonical Python package exposes MjModel, MjData, and mj_step.
Model fields and data arrays are mutable views and values must be copied for historical logs.
The PyPI package includes the MuJoCo library.

sources.title: MuJoCo simulation programming documentation
claims: xfrc_applied represents Cartesian wrenches applied at body centers of mass.
mj_step advances forward dynamics and integration.

sources.title: MuJoCo perturbation-force implementation
claims: xfrc_applied stores force in the first three values and torque in the final three values.

cross_checks: The official engine source was used to resolve an incorrect torque-first assumption.
A short local rollout confirmed that the first three wrench values produce translation.
interpretation: Use one fresh MjModel and MjData per candidate, copy observed arrays before stepping, apply planar force through xfrc_applied[:, 0:2], and compare rollouts using objective metrics.
hypotheses: A small force-duration candidate set can achieve the deterministic planar target without feedback.
The same open-loop plan will not necessarily generalize to changed mass or friction.

validation.protocol: Evaluate three force-duration candidates from fresh state and repeat the winner from another fresh state.
validation.result: The balanced candidate stopped 0.04499 m from the target center; predicted and executed metrics matched.

unresolved_questions: How much mass, friction, and pose variation can the selected plan tolerate?
Should feedback control or online system identification be introduced first?
